canonical.title: Shortest Path in a Binary Matrix (8-Directional)
canonical.sourceFilePath: 13. Graphs/4. Shortest Path Problems/04. Shortest Path in binary matrix.cpp

narrative.title: The Corner-to-Clearance Robot Run
narrative.scenario: A warehouse robot must travel from the north-west corner to the south-east corner of a floor grid. Blocked bays are marked 1 and open bays 0, and the robot may roll in any of the eight directions — including diagonals — across open bays only. The route planner wants the shortest run measured in bays entered, or confirmation that no diagonal-capable route exists.
narrative.inputFormat: An n x n binary matrix grid where 0 is open and 1 is blocked.
narrative.outputFormat: Return the number of cells on the shortest clear path from (0,0) to (n-1,n-1), or -1 if no such path exists.
constraints: grid[0][0] and grid[n-1][n-1] may need checking — the path must start and end on open cells

testCases.explanation: The diagonal hop from corner to corner visits exactly two cells.
The only corridor hugs the top row and the right column: four bays.

hintLevels: Level 1: Uniform step costs plus a single start — a ring-by-ring wave gives the first arrival at the goal.
Level 2: Expand all eight neighbours, guard the borders, and mark visited on enqueue to avoid repeats.
Level 3: Bail out early with -1 if either corner is blocked; the level counter doubles as the cell count.
